authoring_rules: One distinct actor per scenario, so no scenario's grants reach another scenario's items. The shared tenant is unchanged, because the corpus's declared permitted_tenant_ids is what the judge checks against.
Every checkpoint sits on a task the paired scenario already declared in permitted_task_ids. The world adds content and placement; it never widens an audience.

task_resume: required checkpoints carry the scenario's own goal wording, which contains the query term, so lexical recall can reach them. The non-required checkpoint on the same task carries unrelated work.

cross_task_recall: the required checkpoint sits on the second task and states the answer WITHOUT the query term appearing verbatim, so lexical recall misses it and semantic recall has something to add. The home-task checkpoint carries the term but is not a required fact.
These rules were fixed before the world was written and are published here so a reader can check the world against them rather than trusting it. No observation was taken while authoring.
